take_homes: Whatever I put in front of the AI steers the answer. Specific input from me gives a specific result, and vague input gives the average of everyone.
The AI's account of its own work is a claim I check against what I know. It grades its own homework too kindly, so I need a second, cold reader.
A rules file the agent reads every session is the reusable part. It could hold how we write month-end variance commentary.

monday.move: Ask my controller to write down our variance-commentary conventions in a short rules file and try it once on last month's close, with a plan shown before anything is written
monday.stop_condition: If the controller needs more than half a day, or the output is not better than last month's by their own judgement, stop
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, so it only starts on non-sensitive material until they do

misconception.why: The text says the improvement came from how well I fed the model, not from the model, which cuts against buying a licence. But nothing in the day gave me a per-seat cost, a payback figure, or a number showing the organisation's skill grows, so I am still treating it as a purchase until I see one.

one_line: Two useful ideas, that context steers the output and that the AI marks its own work too kindly, buried in forty-five minutes of building a personal website, with no cost or payback anywhere.
